BURSEVI:v10p318/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p318/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p318/r6.claim: The earlier scrolls include those of Abraham and Moses; sahifa means a sheet or written page, while mushaf is a collection of written sheets.
BURSEVI:v10p318/r6.anchor: {صحف} جدك {إبراهيم} الخليل عليه السلام صحف أخيك {موسى} الكليم عليه السلام بدل من الصحف الأولى

QASHANI:87:16-18/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:16-18/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:16-18/r2.claim: This teaching about receptive people benefiting from reminders, the unready suffering, the purified flourishing, and sensory-life seekers perishing is found in the ancient scriptures, preserved in luminous tablets disclosed to the two prophets mentioned.
QASHANI:87:16-18/r2.anchor: المعنى من انتفاع المستعد بالتذكير وعدم انتفاع العديم الاستعداد

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says this sura was copied from the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى قال : نسخت هذه السورة من صحف إبراهيم وموسى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says this sura appears in Abraham's and Moses' scriptures just as it was revealed to Muhammad.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r2.anchor: عن السدى ان هذه السورة في صحف إبراهيم وموسى مثل ما نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the story of this sura is found in the earlier scriptures.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى يقول : قصة هذه السورة في الصحف الاولى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r4.claim: Qatada says God's books came successively with the message that the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى قال : تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون ان الاخرة خير وابقى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r5.claim: Qatada also says the earlier scriptures taught that the Hereafter is better than the world.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى الاية قال : في الصحف الاولى ان الاخرة خير من الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says this teaching is in all God's books.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r6.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى قال : في كتب الله كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r3.claim: The closing statement dignifies this beneficial, enduring teaching as also found in Abraham's and Moses' scriptures, emphasized for deniers familiar with those messengers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r3.anchor: تذييل للكلام وتنويه به بأنه من الكلام النافع الثابت في كتب إبراهيم وموسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r4.claim: “This” refers to the teaching from success through the afterlife's superiority; the earlier opening verses are not what the old scriptures confirm here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r4.anchor: والإشارة بكلمة { هذا } إلى مجموع قوله { قد أفلح من تزكى إلى قوله وأبقى } ( الأعلى : 14 17 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r5.claim: Ibn Mardawayh and al-Ajurri report Abu Dharr asking the Prophet about revelation from Abraham's and Moses' scrolls; the Prophet recited 87:14–17, and Ibn Ashur could not establish the report's grade.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r5.anchor: روى ابن مردويه والآجري عن أبي ذر قال : ( قلت يا رسول الله هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r6.claim: “In the scrolls” means that a counterpart in meaning is written there, using scrolls metonymically for their contents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r6.anchor: ومعنى الظرفية من قوله : { لفي الصحف } أن مماثله في المعنى مكتوب في الصحف الأولى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r7.claim: Ṣuḥuf is an irregular plural of ṣaḥīfa but the more eloquent form; Abraham had scrolls, while Moses had many, comprising the Torah's books.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r7.anchor: و { الصحف } : جمع صحيفة على غير قياس لأن قياس جمعه صحائف ، ولكنه مع كونه غير مقيس هو الأفصح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r8.claim: The wording moves from a general mention to specification: “the scrolls of Abraham and Moses” apposes “the earlier scrolls.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r8.anchor: وجاء نظم الكلام على أسلوب الإجمال والتفصيل ليكون لهذا الخبر مزيد تقرير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r14.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak says “this” refers to the Quran; a report says the Quran was transcribed from the earlier scriptures.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r14.anchor:
قال الضحاك: أراد القرآن، وروي أن القرآن انتسخ من الصحف
الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r15.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Said ibn Jubayr, takes “this” to mean the surah's teachings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r15.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: الإشارة إلى معاني السورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r17.claim: The teaching remained present in every religious law, from the earliest scriptures through later revelations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r17.anchor: أي لم ينسخ هذا قط في شرع من الشرائع فهو في الأولى وفي الأخيرات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r18.claim: A prophetic report says that “if you feel no shame, do as you wish” is among the sayings inherited from the first prophecy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r18.anchor: إن مما أدرك الناس من كلام النبوة الأولى: «إذا لم تستحي فاصنع ما شئت»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r19.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r19.claim: Most readers pronounce the ḥāʾ in al-ṣuḥuf with ḍamma; Harun's report from Abu Amr and al-A'mash use sukūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r19.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «الصحف» مضمومة الحاء، وروى هارون عن أبي عمرو بسكون الحاء، وهي قراءة الأعمش،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r1.claim: One view says “this” refers to the statement that the afterlife is better and more lasting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r1.anchor: أحدها انه قوله تعالى والآخرة خير وأبقى قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r2.claim: A second view takes “this” to refer to the whole sūra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r2.anchor: والثاني هذه السورة قاله عكرمة والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the wording itself need not be in the earlier scriptures; rather, the principle that the successful purify themselves, remember God, and pray is there as in the Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r3.anchor: في الصحف الأولى كما هو في القرآن قاله ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r4.claim: Ibn Jarīr says “this” spans 87:14 through “and more lasting.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92#3/r4.anchor: والرابع أنه من قوله تعالى قد أفلح من تزكى إلى قوله وأبقى قاله ابن جرير

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#3/r1.claim: The verse does not mean the entire sūra’s meaning or exact wording occurred in earlier scriptures; only the teaching that success belongs to one who purifies, remembers God, and prays is shared.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#3/r1.anchor: لم يرد أن معنى السورة في الصحف الأولى، ولا الألفاظ بعينها. وإنما أراد: أن "الفلاح لمن تزكى، وذكر اسم ربه فصلى"

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r3.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r3.claim: Qatāda says “this” in “this is in the earlier scriptures” means the entire sūra and everything stated in it.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r3.anchor: قيل: أراد جميع السورة، وما نص فيها، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r4.speaker: الكلبي
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says “this” means the passage from “successful is the one who purifies himself” to the sūra’s end.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد قوله: (قد أفلح من تزكى) إلى آخر السورة، عن الكلبي

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd takes “this” to mean that the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r5.anchor: يعني قوله: والآخرة خير وأبقى، عن ابن زيد

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r6.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes “this” to mean the Qur’an.

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r7.speaker: أبي علي
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī understands the earlier-scripture reference as God’s admonition and explanation urging preference for the Hereafter.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r7.anchor: ما وعظكم به وبينه لكم لتؤثروا الآخرة على الدنيا، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r8.claim: Other explanations identify “this” as the admonition to obey and avoid sin, the praised status of purification and prayer in earlier scriptures, or the commands given to the communities addressed by their scriptures (Abū Muslim).
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r8.anchor: معناه: هذا الذي ذكرناك ووعظناك به، والترغيب في الطاعة، والنهي عن المعصية

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r11.claim: One saying attributed to Abraham’s scriptures advises the rational person to guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his own affairs; the author also says 104 books were revealed to a list of prophets.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r11.anchor: وقيل: في صحف إبراهيم: (ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r1.claim: This may refer to the teaching from success through the better, lasting Hereafter, or to the entire surah; its meaning is found in earlier scriptures.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى قوله : { قد أفلح } إلى { أبقى }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r2.claim: Abu Dharr reports asking the Prophet about scriptures; the reply counts 104, apportioned among Adam, Seth, Enoch, Abraham, and the four later named books.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه ( أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Abraham's scroll teaches a prudent person to guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his affairs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r3.anchor: في صحف إبراهيم ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r4.claim: A prophetic report promises ten rewards for each letter God revealed to Abraham, Moses, and Muhammad to whoever recites al-A'la.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة الأعلى أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد كل حرف أنزله الله على إبراهيم وموسى ومحمد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r5.speaker: علي وابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r5.claim: When the Prophet recited this surah he said Glory to my Lord the Most High; Ali and Ibn Abbas are also reported to say it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r5.anchor: وكان إذا قرأها قال : سبحان ربي الأعلى وكان علي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r6.claim: The source says the Prophet liked this surah and reports that Michael was the first to say Glory to my Lord the Most High.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r6.anchor: أول من قال ( سبحان ربي الأعلى ) مكيائيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r20.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r20.claim: He says the afterlife's superiority and permanence already appear in earlier scriptures.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r20.anchor: خير وأبقى في الصحف الأولى ، قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r21.claim: A second view says all that God recounted in this sura comes from earlier scriptures.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r22.claim: A third view identifies the earlier scriptures as all of God's revealed books; Wahb ibn Munabbih reports their count and distribution among the prophets.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r23.speaker: وهب بن منبه
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r23.claim: He reports 105 scrolls and four books: 35 scrolls for Seth, 50 for Enoch, 20 for Abraham, and the Torah, Psalms, Gospel, and Furqan for Moses, David, Jesus, and Muhammad.

MUQATIL:87:14-19/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r4.claim: The teaching is found in the earlier scriptures: Ibrahim's scrolls and the books of Moses, meaning the Torah; Ibrahim's scrolls have since been taken away.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#7/r1.claim: “This” points either to the statements that the successful person is purified and the hereafter is better, or to the whole surah; these meanings are present in the earlier scriptures.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#7/r1.anchor: هذا إشارة إلى قوله قد أفلح إلى أبقى أى أن معنى هذا الكلام وأراد فى تلك الصحف

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#7/r2.claim: The claim that this Qur'anic teaching is in earlier scriptures, despite different wording and language, supports the permissibility of reciting the Qur'an in Persian during prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#7/r2.anchor: وهو دليل على جواز قراءة القرآن بالفارسية فى الصلاة لأنه جعله مذكورا فى تلك الصحف

QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r1.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r1.claim: They identify ‘this’ as the teaching that the afterlife is better and more lasting, a truth reiterated throughout God's books.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r1.anchor: قال قتادة وابن زيد: يريد قوله: { والآخرة خير وأبقى }. وقالا: تتابعت كتب الله

QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r2.claim: He takes ‘this’ to mean all of God's scriptures.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: «إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى» قال: كتب الله جل ثناؤه كلها

QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r4.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies ‘this’ as the whole surah.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r4.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس: «إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى» قال: هذه السورة

NAHHAS:v5p207/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r14.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p207/r14.claim: One explanation, apparently Qatāda's, takes the preceding statement that the afterlife is better and lasting as what is in the earlier scriptures.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r14.anchor: أحدها أن قوله جل وعز والآخرة خير وأبقى في الصحف الأولى وهذا كأنه مذهب قتادة

NAHHAS:v5p207/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r15.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p207/r15.claim: Another explanation is that success belongs in the earlier scriptures to those who purify themselves, remember the Lord, and pray.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r15.anchor: وقيل الفلاح لمن تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى في الصحف الأولى

NAHHAS:v5p207/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p207/r17.claim: The author favors Qatāda's nearby-reference reading because a phrase normally refers to what immediately precedes unless decisive evidence redirects it.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r17.anchor: إلا أن قول قتادة حسن لأنه لما يليه وسبيل الشيء أن يكون لما يليه

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r1.claim: The surah's foundational creed is ancient, rooted in the first scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r1.anchor: هذا الذي ورد في هذه السورة وهو يتضمن أصول العقيدة الكبرى

QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r2.claim: Truth and creed are one because their source and the will behind sending messengers are one; details vary with changing needs and eras but return to the same root.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r2.anchor: إنه حق واحد ، يرجع إلى أصل واحد

QUTB-ZILAL:87:19/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:19/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:19/r1.claim: The core truths of this surah were present in Abraham's and Moses' scriptures; the creed's shared source is the Lord who creates, perfects, apportions, and guides.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:19/r1.anchor: إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r1.claim: One view takes this as the whole sura, which includes divine oneness, prophecy, a warning against disbelief, and a promise for obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r1.anchor: جميع السورة ، وذلك لأن السورة مشتملة على التوحيد والنبوة والوعيد على الكفر بالله

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r2.claim: Another view reads 87:14–17 as a sequence: purify intellect and morals, complete the spirit through knowledge of God, complete the limbs through obedience, reject worldly attachment, and seek the afterlife; these truths cross religious laws.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r2.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى تكميل الروح بمعرفة الله تعالى ، وأما قوله : { فصلى }

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r3.claim: Abu Dharr asks whether the teachings occur in Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls; the Prophet tells him to read 87:14.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r3.anchor: روى عن أبي ذر أنه قال : قلت هل في الدنيا مما في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟ فقال : اقرأ يا أبا ذر

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r4.claim: A third view points only to the nearest antecedent, 87:17, and compares the reference to 26:196 and 42:13.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#3/r4.anchor: إن قوله هذا إشارة إلى قوله : { والاخرة خير وأبقى } وذلك لأن الإشارة راجعة إلى أقرب المذكورات

SAMIN-DURR:87:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:18/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr, in al-Aʿmash and Hārūn's transmission, reads both occurrences with a silent ḥāʾ; the form is straightforward.
SAMIN-DURR:87:18/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو في رواية الأعمش وهارون بسكون الحاء في الحرفين

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r1.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r1.claim: The reference to old scriptures may concern the subjects discussed in verses 14–17.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r1.anchor: This refers to either the subjects mentioned in vv. 14–17

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that it refers to the whole of this surah.

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r3.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r3.claim: Another interpretation applies the reference to the entire Quran, as verse 26:196 does.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r3.anchor: or the entire Quran, as in 26:196

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r4.claim: Although Judaism and Christianity do not assign Abraham a revealed book, the Quran and hadith imply that he had a scripture.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r4.anchor: Although Judaism and Christianity do not ascribe a revealed book to Abraham, that Abraham had a particular scripture is implied in both the Quran and the Ḥadīth

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r5.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r5.claim: A report attributes to the Prophet a total of 104 revealed books: 50 to Seth, 30 to Idrīs, 10 to Abraham, 10 to Moses before the Torah, plus Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Quran.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r5.anchor: When the Prophet was asked how many revealed books there were, he responded

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r6.speaker: Shiite sources
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r6.claim: Shiite sources give a slightly different narration, and some say Abraham received 20 scrolls.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r6.anchor: This tradition has a slightly different narration in Shiite sources

TAB:87:19/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r6.speaker: author
TAB:87:19/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the demonstrative covers the nearby verses about purification, prayer, preferring this life, and the better, lasting afterlife, since this is the nearest referent; ṣuḥuf means the books of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:19/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ،   قول من قال :  إن قوله :  قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكى وَذَكَرَ اسمَ رَبّهِ فَصَلّى

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r1.claim: One report takes “this” to refer to the verses in Sūrat al-Aʿlā.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، عن عكرمة، " {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى} [الأعلى: 19] يقول: الآيات التي في سبح اسم ربك الأعلى "

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya interprets “this” as the story of the whole sūra.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r2.anchor: عن الربيع، عن أبي العالية {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى} [الأعلى: 19] قال: «قصة هذه السورة لفي الصحف الأولى»

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r3.claim: Qatāda says the account God has related throughout this sūra was already in the earlier scriptures.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: " {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} [الأعلى: 18] قال: إن هذا الذي قص الله في هذه السورة

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r4.claim: Another report from Qatāda says the teaching that the afterlife is better and more enduring recurs in God’s books.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} [الأعلى: 18] قال: تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون، أن الآخرة خير وأبقى "

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says Abraham’s and Moses’s scriptures taught that the afterlife is better than the first life.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى} [الأعلى: 19] قال: في الصحف التي أنزلها الله على إبراهيم وموسى

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.claim: Ṭabarī prefers that “this” refers to the nearest preceding lines, 87:14–17, because a demonstrative most naturally points to what is nearby; ṣuḥuf means books or scrolls.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.anchor: وإنما قلت: ذلك أولى بالصحة من غيره، لأن هذا إشارة إلى حاضر، فلأن يكون إشارة إلى ما قرب منها

TAB-FULL:v24p325/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p325/r1.speaker: أبو الخلد
TAB-FULL:v24p325/r1.claim: Abū al-Khald reports that Abraham’s scrolls came on Ramadan’s first night, followed by the Torah on the sixth, Psalms on the twelfth, Gospel on the eighteenth, and Qurʾān on the twenty-fourth.
TAB-FULL:v24p325/r1.anchor: عن أبي الخلد، قال: «نزلت صحف إبراهيم في أول ليلة من رمضان، وأنزلت التوراة لست ليال خلون من رمضان

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r2.claim: He takes “this” to refer to the four preceding verses, from the promise of success through the comparison with worldly life.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r2.anchor: الإشارة بهذا إلى ما بين في قوله { قد أفلح من تزكى } إلى تمام أربع آيات

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r3.claim: Another view takes “this” to refer only to the statement that the afterlife is better and more enduring.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r3.anchor: وقيل هذا إشارة إلى مضمون قوله { والآخرة خير وأبقى }

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r4.claim: Calling the scriptures ancient before naming Abraham and Moses is said to magnify their status.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r4.anchor: وفي إبهام الصحف ووصفها بالتقدم أولا ثم بيانها وتفسيرها بصحف إبراهيم وموسى

ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r3.claim: This refers to the statements from verses 14 through 18; another view takes it as referring to the whole sura.
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r3.anchor: يعني من قوله: (قد أفلح من تزكى) إلى هذا الموضع.

THALABI:v10p185/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r8.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v10p185/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the referent is the Qurʾān, which is in the earlier books, namely the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
THALABI:v10p185/r8.anchor: الضحاك: إن هذا القرآن، لفي الصحف الكتب الأولى

THALABI:v10p185/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p185/r9.claim: Ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa, a written sheet.
THALABI:v10p185/r9.anchor: الكتب الأولى واحدتها صحيفة، صحف إبراهيم وموسى يقال

THALABI:v10p185/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p185/r10.claim: A saying attributed to Abraham's scriptures counsels the wise to guard the tongue, know the age, and attend to one's own affairs.
THALABI:v10p185/r10.anchor: يقال: إن في صحف إبراهيم ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه

THALABI:v10p185/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r11.speaker: أبو ذر
THALABI:v10p185/r11.claim: Abū Dharr's report begins with the Prophet saying there were 124,000 prophets and 313 messengers, including four Arab prophets: Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Shuʿayb, and Muḥammad.
THALABI:v10p185/r11.anchor: قلت: يا رسول الله كم الأنبياء؟ قال: «مائة ألف وأربعة وعشرون ألفا

THALABI:v10p186/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p186/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
THALABI:v10p186/r1.claim: The Prophet's report to Abū Dharr says 104 books were revealed: ten sheets to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Enoch/Idrīs, ten to Abraham, plus Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and the Furqān; Idrīs was first to write with a pen.
THALABI:v10p186/r1.anchor: مائة وأربع كتب، منها على آدم عشر صحف، وعلى شيث خمسين صحيفة، وعلى أخنوخ، وهو إدريس

WAHIDI-QT:87:18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:18/r1.claim: The success of the purified and the Hereafter's superiority are recorded in earlier scriptures.
WAHIDI-QT:87:18/r1.anchor: الذي ذكرت من فلاح المتزكي وكون الآخرة خيرا من الدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r2.claim: The preceding teaching about the purified person's success and the afterlife's superiority is present in earlier scriptures.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r2.anchor: الذي ذكرت من فلاح المتزكي، وكون الآخرة خيرا من الدنيا

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r1.claim: The formula about Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls parallels Q 53:36–37; the note also points to the general discussion of Moses in the early Meccan Quran.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r1.anchor: zu der Wendung ṣuḥuf ʾibrāhīm wa-mūsā vgl. 53:36.37

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Ahrens
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r3.claim: Ahrens interprets the scrolls as a rough designation for the Old Testament or the whole Bible because Q 53:36 onward paraphrases biblical material.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Ahrens will die „Schriften Abrahams und Moses“ als „eine ungefähre Bezeichnung des Alten Testaments oder vielmehr der ganzen Bibel“ verstehen

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r4.claim: Despite Abraham not receiving a revealed book in the Old Testament, the pair may summarize biblical scripture through the figures’ prominence; specific apocryphal Abrahamic books are unlikely.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Wie in Q 53 ist vermutlich weniger eine Evokation bestimmter biblischer Einzelschriften intendiert

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r5.speaker: Heck
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r5.claim: Heck likewise reads the genitive objectively, as revealed writings about Moses and Abraham; the author instead sees a broad evocation of biblical tradition rather than specific books.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Heck, „Scrolls“, EQ, der den Genitiv ebenfalls im Sinne eines Genitivus objectivus als über Mose und Abraham berichtende Offenbarungsschriften deutet

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r6.claim: Ṣuḥuf means documents or written sheets, likely borrowed from Old South Arabian; in early Quranic usage its plural names revelation texts or a heavenly archetype, unlike profane pre-Islamic poetry.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r7.claim: Later occurrences at Q 20:133 and 98:2 appear to quote early passages; from Mecca II kitāb replaces ṣuḥuf as the usual term for revelation scripture, alongside zubur.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r7.anchor: Ab Mekka II wird der Ausdruck ṣuḥuf durch das arabische Wort kitāb verdrängt

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r8.claim: Q 73, 74, and 85 also close with confirmation of revelation, while related floating references appear elsewhere; calls can serve as sura endings too.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r8.anchor: Wie der vorliegende Text enden auch Q 73, 74 und 85 mit einer Offenbarungsbestätigung als regelrechtem Surenschluss

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r9.claim: The repeated scroll term links verses 18–19 by concatenation, a device also found in early Quranic passages and pre-Islamic poetry that stretches syntax across short verses.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r9.anchor: Zu der V. 18.19 verbindenden Konkatenation, bei der das Schlusswort eines Verses zu Beginn des folgenden Verses wieder aufgenommen wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r3.claim: The ending authorizes the rebuke by affirming that Quranic proclamation agrees with ancient revealed scriptures associated with Abraham and Moses; the psalm-like opening hymn supports this claim.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r3.anchor: Das Scheltwort in V. 16.17 erfährt eine nachträgliche Autorisierung durch das abschließende Verspaar V. 18.19

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r1.claim: Suhuf is the plural of sahifa, then used synonymously with book, meaning revelation given to prophets; here it refers to books given to Abraham and Moses, examples rather than the limits of revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r1.anchor: her iki âyette yer alan suhuftan maksat, “Hz. İbrâhim ve Hz. Mûsâ’ya verilen kitaplardır. Bu iki peygambere nisbet edilen sahîfeler, geçmiş vahiylerin sadece birer örneğini teşkil eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r2.claim: The principal named scriptures are the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Qur’an; reports assign ten sheets to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Idris, and ten to Abraham.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r2.anchor: Sahîfelerden 10’unun Hz. Âdem’e, 50’sinin Şît’e, 30’unun İdrîs’e, 10’unun da İbrâhim’e verildiği rivayet edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r3.claim: As in 26:196, these verses affirm that revelation to all prophets comes from one divine source and that revealed religions share universal principles of faith, worship, and morality.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r3.anchor: bütün peygamberlere vahyin tek kaynaktan, Allah’tan geldiğini ve ilâhî dinlerin iman, ibadet ve ahlâk konularında aynı prensipleri

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#6/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#6/r1.claim: Qatāda says what this sūra recounts is found in the earlier scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#6/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى ﴾ قال إن ما قص الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r1.claim: The promise that the one who purifies succeeds and that the Hereafter is better was not abrogated: it held in earlier revelations and in the final dispensation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r1.anchor: لفي الصحف الأولى، لم ينسخ إفلاح من تزكى، والآخرة خير وأبقى في شرع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r2.claim: The majority read “ṣuḥuf” with a ḍamma on ḥāʾ; al-Aʿmash, Hārūn, and ʿIṣma report a sukūn, identified as Tamīmī usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: الصحف بضم الحاء كالحرف الثاني والأعمش وهرون وعصمة، كلاهما عن أبي عمرو:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r3.claim: The majority read the name Ibrāhīm; several transmitters report variants, including Abū Rajāʾ without the alif and yāʾ and Abū Mūsā and Ibn al-Zubayr’s “Ibrāhām.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إبراهيم بألف وبياء والهاء مكسورة وأبو رجاء: بحذفهما والهاء مفتوحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r4.claim: The discussion of the scrolls of Abraham and Moses was already given in Sūrat al-Najm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p459/r4.anchor: وتقدم في والنجم الكلام على صحف إبراهيم وموسى عليهما الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd, with Qatāda also reported, takes “this” to refer to the statement that the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r1.anchor: إشارة على ما أخرج أبن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن زيد إلى قوله تعالى والآخرة خير وأبقى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r2.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r2.claim: Other interpreters refer “this” to the earlier statement that the successful person purifies, remembers the Lord, and prays; a later hadith is said to support this.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r2.anchor: وقال غير واحد إشارة إلى ما ذكر من قوله سبحانه قد أفلح من تزكى الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes “this” as the Qur'an, relating the verse to the statement that it is in the scriptures of the earlier peoples.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك إشارة إلى القرآن فالآية كقوله تعالى وأنه لفي زبر الأولين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and al-Suddī refer it to the teachings contained across the sūrahs; al-Ālūsī considers this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وعكرمة والسدي إشارة إلى ما تضمنته السور جميعا وفيه بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r5.speaker: الأعمش وهارون وعصمة عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r5.claim: These readers give sukūn to the hāʾ in ṣuḥuf here and in the next verse, a Tamīm dialect.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وهارون وعصمة كلاهما عن أبي عمرو بسكون الحاء وكذا فيما بعد وهي لغة تميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r1.claim: ‘This’ refers to the preceding four verses: the earlier scriptures taught that the purified and praying prosper, people favor worldly life, and the afterlife is better and more lasting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r1.anchor: ما ذكر من قوله: "قد أفلح من تزكى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r3.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet recited al-Aʿla and al-Kafirun in the two rakʿas before witr, then al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and al-Nas in witr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r3.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r8.claim: “This” refers to the preceding promise of success, which gathers the religion's central teaching and the essence of revealed books.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r8.anchor: الإشارة إلى ما سبق من { قد أفلح } فإنه جامع أمر الديانة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r1.claim: This refers to the great admonition of glorification, purification, remembrance, prayer, and turning from the world toward the afterlife; it gathers all good and belongs to every revealed law, so its aim cannot be abrogated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r1.anchor: أي الوعظ العظيم بالتسبيح الذي ذكر في هذه السور وما تأثر عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r2.claim: The Quran preserves unsurpassed eloquence, genres of poetry, legal limits, and unseen knowledge, surpassing poets and soothsayers and showing Muhammad follows earlier messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r2.anchor: فإن القرآن جمع المديح الفائق والنسيب الرقيق

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the verses were revealed, the Prophet said the whole message was in Abraham’s and Moses’s scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r4.anchor: قال: لما نزلت {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى} قال: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: هي كلها في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this sūra is in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; one version includes the end of sūra 53 as well.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} قال: نسخت هذه السورة من صحف إبراهيم وموسى

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says this sūra was present in Abraham’s and Moses’s scrolls as it was revealed to the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r6.anchor: عن السدي أن هذه السورة في صحف إبراهيم وموسى مثل ما نزلت على النبي

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the story of this sūra appears in the earlier scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} يقول: قصة هذه السورة في الصحف الأولى

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r8.claim: Qatāda says God’s scriptures agree in succession that the afterlife is better and more enduring.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r8.anchor: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} قال: تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون إن الآخرة خير وأبقى

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r9.claim: Qatāda also specifies that the earlier scrolls teach that the afterlife is better than worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r9.anchor: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} الآية قال: في الصحف الأولى إن الآخرة خير من الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r10.claim: ʿIkrima takes “this” in the verse to mean the verses themselves.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r10.anchor: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} قال: هو الآيات

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the message is found in all of God’s books.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r1.anchor: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} قال: في كتب الله كلها

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r2.claim: In Abū Dharr’s report, the Prophet counts 104 revealed books: fifty to Seth, thirty to Idrīs, ten to Abraham, ten to Moses before the Torah, then the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Qurʾān.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال: قلت يا رسول الله كم أنزل الله من كتاب قال مائة كتاب وأربعة كتب

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r3.claim: The Prophet describes Abraham’s scrolls as collections of maxims: a ruler must answer the oppressed, and a rational person divides time among worship, self-accounting, and lawful needs.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r3.anchor: فما كانت صحف إبراهيم قال: أمثال كلها أيها الملك المتسلط المبتلي المغرور

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r4.claim: The Abrahamic maxims counsel guarding one’s time and tongue, speaking little except usefully, and seeking livelihood, provision for the afterlife, and lawful enjoyment.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r4.anchor: وعلى العاقل أن يكون بصيرا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه حافظا للسانه

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r5.claim: The Prophet calls Moses’s scrolls lessons, challenging the cheerful, laughing, self-assured amid worldly change, strenuous despite destiny, and inactive despite certainty of judgment.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r5.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله: فما كانت صحف موسى قال: كانت عبرا كلها عجبت لمن أيقن بالموت

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.claim: Asked whether the Prophet received anything from those scrolls, he recited the passage from purification and prayer through the superiority of the afterlife and the scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.anchor: هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى قال: يا أبا ذر نعم {قد أفلح من تزكى

ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r1.speaker: ابن زيد وابن جرير
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarīr take this to refer to the statement that the purified succeed and people prefer worldly life; Abū Ḥayyān favors this because the referent is nearby.
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r1.anchor: قاله ابن زيد وابن جرير ،   ويرجح

ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والسدي
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrimah, and al-Suddī take this to refer to the sūra's teachings.

ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r3.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the referent is the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك : إلى القرآن . وقال قتادة

ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r4.claim: Qatādah identifies the referent as the statement that the afterlife is better and more lasting.
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة : إلى قوله : { والآخرة خير وأبقى }

ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r5.claim: The success of the purified and the superiority and permanence of the afterlife were never abrogated: they appeared in earlier scriptures and remain in the final law.
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r5.anchor: لم ينسخ إفلاح من تزكى ،   والآخرة خير وأبقى في شرع

ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r6.claim: The majority pronounce the ḥāʾ in al-ṣuḥuf with ḍamma.

ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r7.speaker: الأعمش وهرون وعصمة عن أبي عمرو
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Hārūn, and ʿIṣmah, both transmitting from Abū ʿAmr, read the word with a quiescent ḥāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r7.anchor: والأعمش وهرون وعصمة ،   كلاهما عن أبي عمرو : بسكونها

ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r8.speaker: كتاب اللوامح العبقلي عن أبي عمرو
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r8.claim: Al-Lawāmiʿ al-ʿAqbali reports Abū ʿAmr reading both forms with a quiescent ḥāʾ, a Tamīm dialect.
ABUHAYYAN:87:18/r8.anchor: وفي كتاب اللوامح العبقلي عن أبي عمرو : الصحف صحف بإسكان الحاء فيهما

ALUSI:87:18/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:18/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI:87:18/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd, reported by Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, identifies this with the teaching that the Hereafter is better and more enduring; this is also transmitted from Qatādah.
ALUSI:87:18/r1.anchor: على ما أخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن زيد إلى قوله تعالى

ALUSI:87:18/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:18/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:87:18/r2.claim: Qatādah is also reported to identify this as the teaching that the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
ALUSI:87:18/r2.anchor: وروى ذلك عن قتادة وقال غير واحد إشارة إلى ما ذكر من قوله سبحانه

ALUSI:87:18/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:18/r3.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI:87:18/r3.claim: Several commentators take this to refer to the material beginning successful indeed is the one who purifies himself; a forthcoming hadith supports this reading.
ALUSI:87:18/r3.anchor: وقال غير واحد إشارة إلى ما ذكر من قوله سبحانه { قد أفلح من تزكى }

ALUSI:87:18/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:18/r4.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI:87:18/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says this refers to the Qurʾān, comparing the statement with 26:196.
ALUSI:87:18/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك إشارة إلى القرآن فالآية كقوله تعالى

ALUSI:87:18/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:18/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والسدي
ALUSI:87:18/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrimah, and al-Suddī take this to refer to the contents of all sūrahs; al-Ālūsī considers it far-fetched.
ALUSI:87:18/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وعكرمة والسدي إشارة إلى ما تضمنته السور جميعاً وفيه بعد

ALUSI:87:18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:18/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:18/r6.claim: The teaching or referent is established in the earlier scriptures in meaning.

ALUSI:87:18/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:18/r7.speaker: الأعمش وهرون وعصمة عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI:87:18/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Hārūn, and ʿIṣmah, transmitting from Abū ʿAmr, read al-ṣuḥuf with sukūn on ḥāʾ; this is a Tamīm dialect.
ALUSI:87:18/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وهرون وعصمة كلاهما عن أبي عمرو بسكون الحاء وكذا فيما بعد

BAGHAWI:87:18/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:18/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:18/r1.claim: “This” means the preceding four verses, from the success of the one who purifies himself through the preference for worldly life; earlier scriptures also mention the purifier's success, prayer, and the superior, lasting Hereafter.
BAGHAWI:87:18/r1.anchor: { إن هذا } يعني ما ذكر من قوله : { قد أفلح من تزكى } إلى أربع آيات ، { لفي الصحف الأولى }

BAYDAWI:87:18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:18/r1.claim: “This” points to the preceding declaration that the successful person is purified; it sums up religion and the revealed scriptures.
BAYDAWI:87:18/r1.anchor: إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى الإشارة إلى ما سبق من قد أفلح فإنه جامع أمر الديانة وخلاصة الكتب المنزلة

BIQAI:87:18/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:18/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:18/r1.claim: This means the great admonition of these sūras: glorification leading to purification through remembrance, prayer, turning from the world, and turning toward the Hereafter; it is the unalterable aim of every law.
BIQAI:87:18/r1.anchor: أي الوعظ العظيم بالتسبيح الذي ذكر

BIQAI:87:18/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:18/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:18/r2.claim: The ancient scriptures' long acceptance lends authority and makes souls more receptive; this confirms Muhammad follows earlier prophets' way, so an impartial person cannot single him out for rejection.
BIQAI:87:18/r2.anchor: ما مضت عليه السنون ومرت على قبوله الدهور

BIQAI:87:18/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:18/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:18/r3.claim: The Qur'an surpasses poets and soothsayers through eloquent praise, love poetry, heroic boasting, satire, exhortation, warning, narratives, and legal rulings, as well as reports of past and future unseen matters.
BIQAI:87:18/r3.anchor: فاستراح من ضلال الشعراء والكهان ، الموقعين في الإثم والعدوان

DURR:87:18/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that, when these verses were revealed, the Prophet said all of this is contained in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
DURR:87:18/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : لما نزلت { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى } قال : رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:18/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:18/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says this surah was transcribed from the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; another wording extends the material to al-Najm 53:37 through the end of that surah.
DURR:87:18/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى } قال : نسخت هذه السورة من صحف إبراهيم وموسى

DURR:87:18/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR:87:18/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says this surah is found in Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls just as it was revealed to Muhammad.
DURR:87:18/r3.anchor: عن السدي أن هذه السورة في صحف إبراهيم وموسى مثل ما نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:18/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:18/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliyah explains “this” as the story or account of this surah, which was present in earlier scrolls.
DURR:87:18/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى } يقول : قصة هذه السورة في الصحف الأولى .

DURR:87:18/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:18/r5.claim: Qatada says God’s books succeed one another in teaching, as heard here: the hereafter is better and more enduring than the world.
DURR:87:18/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى } قال : تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون

DURR:87:18/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:18/r6.claim: Qatada specifies the teaching in the earlier scrolls as the superiority of the hereafter over worldly life.
DURR:87:18/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى } الآية ، قال : في الصحف الأولى إن الآخرة خير

DURR:87:18/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:87:18/r7.claim: Ikrimah identifies “this” as the verses of the surah.
DURR:87:18/r7.anchor: وأخرج الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن عكرمة

DURR:87:18/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR:87:18/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the teaching is found in all of God’s books.
DURR:87:18/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:18/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r9.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR:87:18/r9.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet counted 100 books and four scriptures: fifty scrolls for Seth, thirty for Enoch, ten for Abraham, and ten for Moses before the Torah.
DURR:87:18/r9.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال : «قلت يا رسول الله كم أنزل الله من كتاب ؟ قال مائة كتاب وأربعة كتب

DURR:87:18/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r10.claim: In Abu Dharr’s report, the Prophet’s Abrahamic scroll sayings warn rulers against hoarding, command answering the oppressed even if unbelieving, and commend time for worship, self-examination, lawful needs, careful speech, and lawful provision or enjoyment.
DURR:87:18/r10.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله : فما كانت صحف إبراهيم ؟ قال : أمثال كلها أيها الملك المتسلط المبتلي

DURR:87:18/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r11.claim: The Prophet describes Moses’ scrolls as admonitions against joy despite certainty of death, trust in a changing world, striving despite belief in destiny, and failing to act despite belief in judgment.
DURR:87:18/r11.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله : فما كانت صحف موسى ؟ قال : كانت عبراً كلها عجبت لمن أيقن بالموت

DURR:87:18/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r12.claim: Asked whether any teaching from those scrolls was revealed to him, the Prophet cites the verses from “the one who purifies himself” through this statement about the earlier scrolls.
DURR:87:18/r12.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله : هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟ قال : يا أبا ذر نعم

DURR:87:18/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r13.claim: A report from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shabrah says the Prophet prescribed three rakʿahs for witr, reciting this surah, al-Kafirun, and al-Ikhlas.
DURR:87:18/r13.anchor: يا رسول الله كم توتر ؟ قال : بثلاث ركعات تقرأ فيها ب { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى }

DURR:87:18/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r14.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Harith reports that the Prophet recited this surah in the first rakʿah of a Maghrib prayer and al-Kafirun in the second.
DURR:87:18/r14.anchor: عن عبدالله بن الحارث بن عبد المطلب قال : صلاة صلاها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنا المغرب فقرأ في الركعة الأولى

IBNASHUR:87:18/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:18/r1.claim: This is a concluding amplification that honors the teaching as enduring guidance from the books of Abraham and Moses; the emphatic particles address deniers.
IBNASHUR:87:18/r1.anchor: تذييل للكلام وتنويه به بأنه من الكلام النافع الثابت في كتب إبراهيم وموسى

IBNASHUR:87:18/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:18/r2.claim: “This” refers to the teaching in verses 14–17, not the opening of the sūra through verse 13, whose meaning is not established in Abraham’s and Moses’ books.
IBNASHUR:87:18/r2.anchor: إلى مجموع قوله { قد أفلح من تزكى إلى قوله وأبقى }

IBNASHUR:87:18/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNASHUR:87:18/r3.claim: Abū Dharr asked the Prophet whether anything from Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls had been revealed to him; the Prophet answered with verses 14–17. Ibn ʿĀshūr could not assess the report’s grade.
IBNASHUR:87:18/r3.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال :  « قلت يا رسول الله هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان

IBNASHUR:87:18/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:18/r4.claim: “In the scrolls” means that equivalent content was written in them; the container stands metonymically for what it contains, as in the reference to one’s record.
IBNASHUR:87:18/r4.anchor: أن مماثله في المعنى مكتوب في الصحف الأولى

IBNASHUR:87:18/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:18/r5.claim: Ṣuḥuf is a nonstandard plural of ṣaḥīfa, but more eloquent than the regular ṣaḥāʾif, like sufُن for safīna.
IBNASHUR:87:18/r5.anchor: جمع صحيفة على غير قياس لأن قياس جمعه صحائف

IBNASHUR:87:18/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:18/r6.claim: The plural fits because Abraham had scrolls and Moses had many, collectively represented by the scrolls of the Torah books.
IBNASHUR:87:18/r6.anchor: ووجه جمع الصحف أن إبراهيم كانت له صحف وأن موسى كانت له صحف كثيرة

IBNASHUR:87:18/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:18/r7.claim: The wording uses summary followed by detail to reinforce the claim: “the scrolls of Abraham and Moses” apposes “the earlier scrolls.”
IBNASHUR:87:18/r7.anchor: وجاء نظم الكلام على أسلوب الإجمال والتفصيل ليكون لهذا الخبر مزيد تقرير

IBNASHUR:87:18/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:18/r8.claim: Al-ūlā is a feminine adjective for the broken plural ṣuḥuf, which is treated as feminine.
IBNASHUR:87:18/r8.anchor: و { الأولى } : وصف لصحف الذي هو جمع تكسير

IBNASHUR:87:18/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:18/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:18/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reports three analyses for the roots and form of awwal: hamza-wāw-lām, wāw-wāw-lām with an added hamza, or wāw-hamza-lām with metathesis; ūlā’s derivation varies accordingly.
IBNASHUR:87:18/r9.anchor: واختلف في الحروف الأصلية للفظ أول فقيل : حروفه الأصول

IBNATIYYA:87:18/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes this to refer to the Qurʾān.

IBNATIYYA:87:18/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r2.claim: A report says the Qurʾān was copied from the earlier scriptures.
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r2.anchor: وروي أن القرآن انتسخ من { الصحف الأولى }

IBNATIYYA:87:18/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbās, says this refers to the sūra's meanings.
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس : الإشارة إلى معاني السورة

IBNATIYYA:87:18/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says this refers to the two preceding teachings: success through purification and preferring the world despite the afterlife's superiority; the author prefers this for its proximity.
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : الإشارة إلى هذين الخبرين «إفلاح من تزكى » وإيثار الناس للدنيا مع فضل الآخرة عليها ، وهذا هو الأرجح لقرب المشار إليه بهذا

IBNATIYYA:87:18/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r5.claim: These teachings were never abrogated in any revealed law and appear in both the earliest and later scriptures.
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r5.anchor: أي لم ينسخ هذا قط في شرع من الشرائع فهو في الأولى وفي الأخيرات

IBNATIYYA:87:18/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r6.claim: A Prophetic saying that one may do as one wishes if unashamed is cited as teaching inherited from the earliest prophets and continued thereafter.
IBNATIYYA:87:18/r6.anchor: ونظير هذا قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن مما أدرك الناس من كلام النبوة الأولى : «إذا لم تستحي فاصنع ما شئت

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said all this, or this, was in Abraham’s and Moses’ scriptures. Al-Bazzar says he knows no other connected report through trustworthy transmitters on this route except one previously cited.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت : { إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الأُولَى صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى } قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r2.claim: Al-Nasa’i reports Ibn Abbas saying that all of Surah al-A‘la was in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses; when 53:37 was revealed, he connected Abraham’s fulfillment with the teaching that no bearer bears another’s burden.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت { سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأَعْلَى } قال : كلها في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ، فلما نزلت : { وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى }

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir links this statement to the scroll teachings in 53:36–42: Abraham’s fulfillment, personal responsibility, human striving and its recompense, and the final return to God.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r3.anchor: يعني أن هذه الآية كقوله في سورة  " النجم "  : { أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَى وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r4.claim: Ikrima identifies “this” as the verses in Surah al-A‘la.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة - في قوله : { إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الأُولَى صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى } يقول : الآيات التي في سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the story of this surah is contained in the earlier scriptures.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية : قصة هذه السورة في الصحف الأولى

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir takes “this” to refer to the content of 87:14–17: success through purification, remembrance and prayer, the preference for worldly life, and the better, lasting afterlife.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r6.anchor: واختار ابن جرير أن المراد بقوله : { إِنَّ هَذَا } إشارة إلى قوله : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Ibn Jarir’s reading a good, strong choice.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r7.anchor: وهذا اختيار حسن قوي . وقد روي عن قتادة وابن زيد

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r8.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r8.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd are also reported to hold the view that “this” refers to the passage about purification, worship, and the preference for the lasting afterlife.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r8.anchor: وقد روي عن قتادة وابن زيد ، نحوُه . والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said all this, or this, was in Abraham’s and Moses’ scriptures. Al-Bazzar says he knows no other connected report through trustworthy transmitters on this route except one previously cited.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت : { إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الأُولَى صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى } قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
