IBNKATHIR:87:19/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir takes “this” to refer to the content of 87:14–17: success through purification, remembrance and prayer, the preference for worldly life, and the better, lasting afterlife.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r6.anchor: واختار ابن جرير أن المراد بقوله : { إِنَّ هَذَا } إشارة إلى قوله : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Ibn Jarir’s reading a good, strong choice.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r7.anchor: وهذا اختيار حسن قوي . وقد روي عن قتادة وابن زيد

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r8.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r8.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd are also reported to hold the view that “this” refers to the passage about purification, worship, and the preference for the lasting afterlife.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r8.anchor: وقد روي عن قتادة وابن زيد ، نحوُه . والله أعلم

KASHSHAF:87:18/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:18/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:18/r1.claim: “This” points to the passage from “he succeeds” through “more lasting,” whose meaning is also found in the earlier scriptures.
KASHSHAF:87:18/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى قوله : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } إلى { أبقى } يعني أنّ معنى هذا الكلام وارد في تلك الصحف .

KASHSHAF:87:18/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:18/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:87:18/r2.claim: An alternative says “this” refers to everything in the sūra.
KASHSHAF:87:18/r2.anchor: وقيل : إلى ما في السورة كلها .

MAWARDI:87:18/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:18/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:87:18/r1.claim: Qatāda says that the teaching that the Hereafter is better and more enduring was in the earlier scriptures.
MAWARDI:87:18/r1.anchor: أحدها : يعني أن الآخرة خير وأبقى في الصحف الأولى ، قاله قتادة

MAWARDI:87:18/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:18/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:18/r2.claim: Another view is that what God recounts in this sūra is found in the earlier scriptures.
MAWARDI:87:18/r2.anchor: أن ما قصه الله في هذه السورة هو من الصحف الأولى

MAWARDI:87:18/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:18/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:18/r3.claim: A third view identifies the earlier scriptures with all of God’s revealed books.

MAWARDI:87:18/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:18/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
MAWARDI:87:18/r4.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih reports 105 scriptures and four books: 35 scriptures to Seth, 50 to Idrīs, 20 to Abraham, and the Torah, Psalms, Gospel, and Qurʾān to Moses, David, Jesus, and Muhammad.
MAWARDI:87:18/r4.anchor: وحكى وهب بن منبه في المبتدأ أن جميع الكتب التي أنزلها الله على أنبيائه مائة صحيفة

NASAFI:87:18/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:18/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:18/r1.claim: “This” may refer to the teaching from success through permanence in verses 87:9–17, or to the whole sura; its meaning occurs in the earlier scriptures.
NASAFI:87:18/r1.anchor: هذا إشارة إلى قوله { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } إلى { أبقى } أي أن معنى هذا الكلام وارد في تلك الصحف

NASAFI:87:18/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:18/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:18/r2.claim: Nasafi treats this as evidence that Qur'an may be recited in Persian during prayer although the earlier scriptures lacked its wording or language.
NASAFI:87:18/r2.anchor: وهو دليل على جواز قراءة القرآن بالفارسية في الصلاة لأنه جعله مذكوراً في تلك الصحف

QURTUBI:87:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:18/r1.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
QURTUBI:87:18/r1.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd take this to mean the teaching that the afterlife is better and more lasting; God's books repeatedly affirm it.
QURTUBI:87:18/r1.anchor: قال قتادة وابن زيد : يريد قوله " والآخرة خير وأبقى " .

QURTUBI:87:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:18/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:87:18/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan understands the earlier scriptures to mean all the books of God.
QURTUBI:87:18/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن : " إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى " قال : كتب الله جل ثناؤه كلها

QURTUBI:87:18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:18/r3.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI:87:18/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says this refers to the passage from qad aflaḥa through the end of the sūra, citing the forthcoming Abū Dharr report.
QURTUBI:87:18/r3.anchor: الكلبي : " إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى " من قوله : " قد أفلح " إلى آخر السورة

QURTUBI:87:18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:18/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:18/r4.claim: ʿIkrima reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that this means the whole sūra.
QURTUBI:87:18/r4.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس : " إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى " قال : هذه السورة

QURTUBI:87:18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:18/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:87:18/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes this to mean that the Quran is present in earlier books.
QURTUBI:87:18/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك : إن هذا القرآن لفي الصحف الأولى ، أي الكتب الأولى

RAZI:87:18/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:18/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI:87:18/r1.claim: One view takes “this” to mean the whole sūra, which contains monotheism, prophethood, threats for unbelief, and promises for obedience.
RAZI:87:18/r1.anchor: منهم من قال : جميع السورة ، وذلك لأن السورة مشتملة على التوحيد والنبوة

RAZI:87:18/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:18/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI:87:18/r2.claim: Another view takes “this” to begin at 87:14: cleansing the theoretical faculty of false beliefs and the practical faculty of blameworthy traits.
RAZI:87:18/r2.anchor: بل المشار إليه بهذه الإشارة هو من قوله : { قد أفلح من تزكى } إشارة إلى تطهير النفس

RAZI:87:18/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:18/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI:87:18/r3.claim: On this reading, remembering God completes the spirit through knowledge of Him, prayer adorns the limbs through obedience, worldly preference is censured, and the afterlife and God’s reward are encouraged.
RAZI:87:18/r3.anchor: وأما قوله : { وذكر اسم ربه } فهو إشارة إلى تكميل الروح بمعرفة الله تعالى

RAZI:87:18/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:18/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI:87:18/r4.claim: The matters in this reading do not vary between religious laws, which explains why they were in earlier scriptures; Rāzī says reason and transmitted evidence support it.
RAZI:87:18/r4.anchor: وهذه أمور لا يجوز أن تختلف باختلاف الشرائع ، فلهذا السبب قال : { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى }

RAZI:87:18/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:18/r5.speaker: أبو ذر
RAZI:87:18/r5.claim: Abū Dharr reports being asked whether the Qurʾān contains what is in Abraham’s and Moses’s scriptures and being told to read “Successful is whoever purifies himself.”
RAZI:87:18/r5.anchor: روي عن أبي ذر أنه قال : قلت هل في الدنيا مما في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟

RAZI:87:18/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:18/r6.speaker: آخرون
RAZI:87:18/r6.claim: Another group takes “this” to refer only to the nearest preceding statement, that the afterlife is better and more enduring.
RAZI:87:18/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون : إن قوله { هذا } إشارة إلى قوله : { والآخرة خير وأبقى }

RAZI:87:18/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:18/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:87:18/r7.claim: The reference to earlier scriptures is comparable to the Qurʾānic statements that it is in the earlier books and that God prescribed Noah’s religion.
RAZI:87:18/r7.anchor: فهو نظير لقوله : { وإنه لفي زبر الأولين } وقوله : { شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا }

TAB:87:18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:18/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:87:18/r1.claim: Ikrima says the demonstrative refers to the verses of Sūrat al-Aʿlā, found in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:18/r1.anchor: عن عكرِمة إنّ هَذَا لفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى

TAB:87:18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:18/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB:87:18/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the reference as the story of this sūra, present in the earlier scriptures.
TAB:87:18/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية إن هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى

TAB:87:18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:18/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:18/r3.claim: Qatada says the account God relates in this sūra is also in the earlier scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:18/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى

TAB:87:18/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:18/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:18/r4.claim: Another report from Qatada specifies the teaching that the Hereafter is better and more lasting, repeated across God's books.
TAB:87:18/r4.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى قال :  تتابعت كتب الله

TAB:87:18/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:18/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:87:18/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the scriptures revealed to Abraham and Moses taught that the latter life is better than the first.
TAB:87:18/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى

TAB:87:18/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:18/r6.speaker: author
TAB:87:18/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that 87:14–17 are in the earlier scriptures of Abraham and Moses, since “this” points to nearby material rather than something remote.
TAB:87:18/r6.anchor: لأن هذا إشارة إلى حاضر ،   فلأن يكون إشارة إلى ما قرب منها

TAB:87:18/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:18/r7.speaker: author
TAB:87:18/r7.claim: Al-ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa and refers here to the books of Abraham and Moses.

TAB:87:18/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:18/r8.speaker: أبو الخلد
TAB:87:18/r8.claim: Abū al-Khald reports that Abraham's scriptures came on Ramadan's first night, the Torah on its sixth, Psalms on its twelfth, Gospel on its eighteenth, and Furqān on its twenty-fourth.
TAB:87:18/r8.anchor: عن قتادة ،   عن أبي الخلد ،   قال :  نزلت صحف إبراهيم في أول ليلة من رمضان

BURHAN:v2p38/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p38/r13.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
BURHAN:v2p38/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī says erased recitation and script result when God causes people to forget it and orders them to stop reciting and writing it, as with earlier scriptures; no Qur'anic passage can be abrogated after the Prophet's death.
BURHAN:v2p38/r13.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الرازي نسخ الرسم والتلاوة إنما يكون بأن ينسيهم الله إياه ويرفعه من أوهامهم ويأمرهم بالإعراض عن تلاوته وكتبه في المصحف

ITQAN:v3p69/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r1.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v3p69/r1.claim: Some deny abrogation of recitation on the basis of solitary reports, which cannot establish with certainty that Qur'an was revealed and then abrogated.
ITQAN:v3p69/r1.anchor: حكى القاضي أبو بكر في الانتصار عن قوم إنكار هذا الضرب لأن الأخبار فيه أخبار آحاد ولا يجوز القطع

ITQAN:v3p69/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
ITQAN:v3p69/r2.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi says abrogation of written text and recitation occurs through divinely induced forgetting, so the wording fades like earlier scriptures; any such abrogation must occur by the Prophet's death, since Qur'an cannot be abrogated afterward.
ITQAN:v3p69/r2.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الرازي نسخ الرسم والتلاوة إنما يكون بأن ينسيهم الله إياه ويرفعه من أوهامهم ويأمرهم بالإعراض عن تلاوته وكتبه في المصحف فيندرس

ITQAN:v3p69/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r3.speaker: البرهان
ITQAN:v3p69/r3.claim: The Burhan reads Umar's statement as implying that writing the stoning verse was permissible and therefore that it should have been established in the written text.
ITQAN:v3p69/r3.anchor: وقال في البرهان في قول عمر لولا أن يقول الناس زاد عمر في كتاب الله لكتبتها

ITQAN:v3p69/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r4.speaker: قول
ITQAN:v3p69/r4.claim: A counterargument says Umar would have written the verse if its recitation remained, since public criticism should not have stopped him.
ITQAN:v3p69/r4.anchor: وقد يقال لو كانت التلاوة باقية لبادر عمر ولم يعرج على مقالة الناس لأن مقالة الناس لا تصلح مانعا

ITQAN:v3p69/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p69/r5.claim: The inference from Umar's statement to the continued recitation of the verse is problematic.
ITQAN:v3p69/r5.anchor: وبالجملة هذه الملازمة مشكلة ولعله كان يعتقد أنه خبر واحد والقرآن لا يثبت به

ITQAN:v3p69/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r6.speaker: ابن ظفر
ITQAN:v3p69/r6.claim: Ibn Zafar rejects classifying the stoning text as abrogated recitation because a solitary report cannot establish Qur'an; he calls it al-munsaʾ rather than naskh, a distinction whose wording may be known.
ITQAN:v3p69/r6.anchor: ومن هنا أنكر ابن ظفر في ( الينبوع ) عد هذا مما نسخ تلاوته قال لأن خبر الواحد لا يثبت القرآن

ITQAN:v3p69/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r7.speaker: ابن ظفر
ITQAN:v3p69/r7.claim: Ibn Zafar calls this al-munsaʾ rather than abrogation, noting the categories can be confused and that the wording of al-munsaʾ may be known.
ITQAN:v3p69/r7.anchor: قال وإنما هذا المنسأ لا النسخ وهما مما يلتبسان والفرق بينهما أن المنسأ لفظه قد يعلم حكمه

ITQAN:v3p69/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p69/r8.claim: The suggestion that Umar regarded the stoning text as a solitary report is rejected: it is sound that he received it from the Prophet.
ITQAN:v3p69/r8.anchor: وقوله ( لعله كان يعتقد أنه خبر واحد ) مردود فقد صح أنه تلقاها من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v3p69/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r9.speaker: كثير بن الصامت
ITQAN:v3p69/r9.claim: Kathir ibn al-Salt reports that Zayd ibn Thabit quoted the Prophet's stoning wording while he and Sa'id ibn al-As were writing the codex; Umar said he had asked the Prophet to write it, then explained the distinction between cases warranting lashes and stoning.
ITQAN:v3p69/r9.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم من طريق كثير بن الصامت قال كان زيد بن ثابت وسعيد بن العاص يكتبان المصحف فمرا على هذه الآية

ITQAN:v3p38/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p38/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p38/r1.claim: Order can follow revelation chronology, as in naming the scriptures of Abraham and Moses or placing Torah and Gospel before the Criterion.
ITQAN:v3p38/r1.anchor: أو باعتبار الإنزال كقوله ﴿ صحف إبراهيم وموسى ﴾

ITQAN:v4p535#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the verse about this teaching being in the earlier scriptures was revealed, the Prophet said that this, or all of it, was in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r2.anchor: وأخرج البزار عن ابن عباس قال لما نزلت ﴿ إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى ﴾ قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v1p115/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p115/r1.speaker: عكرمة
ITQAN:v1p115/r1.claim: Ikrima explains the phrase about the earlier scriptures as referring to these verses.
ITQAN:v1p115/r1.anchor: وقال الفريابي نبأنا سفيان عن أبيه عن عكرمة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.claim: Disbelievers prefer transient life to the better, eternal afterlife, so the Prophet's message finds no root in their hearts despite its continuity with earlier prophetic teaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.anchor: giving preference to this world over the next

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r3.claim: The Prophet's teaching is not new: earlier revelation taught that the Hereafter is real life and each soul bears its own deeds and burden.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r3.anchor: whatever the Prophet (sws) is telling his addressees is not something new or unique

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r1.claim: Moses' and Israelite prophets' scriptures survive in the Bible despite substantial alteration; they still clearly teach monotheism and the Hereafter and can revive faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r1.anchor: all of these very clearly and very effectively depict the teachings of monotheism and life in the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r2.claim: Abraham left oral exhortations rather than a scripture; his Israelite descendants preserved the teachings in writing, and their prophets renewed them, with evidence still present in scripture and the Qur'an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r2.anchor: did not leave a scripture for the guidance of his people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r3.claim: The unlettered Ishmaelites preserved Abraham's teaching orally for a time, then lost it to neglect and innovations; Muhammad revived and completed it as God's enduring perfect religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r3.anchor: these teachings were not only revived, they were also completed
